marta: Quick bring-up summary for Cobalt9b quant runs — TL;DR: int8 looks promising for GTN canary but has a ~1pt quality hit vs fp16. Need ops + product guidance on whether to default int8 + fallback, or keep fp16 for canary. Full numbers below.

marta: Baseline (Cobalt9b fp16): p50=110ms p95=220ms, decode=120 tok/s, cost= $0.045 / 1k out tokens, GTN-CORE acc=86.2%

marta: int8 (dynamic quant): p50=95ms p95=200ms, decode=140 tok/s, cost= $0.034 / 1k, acc=85.1% (delta -1.1pp)

marta: int4 (aggressive): p50=75ms p95=210ms, decode=165 tok/s, cost= $0.022 / 1k, acc=82.5% (delta -3.7pp)

marta: 13b fp16 (serving comparator): cost= $0.065 / 1k, acc=88.0% — used as high-accuracy fallback in our sims.

marta: Simulated hybrid routing (70% 9b-int8 + 30% 13b-fp16) => effective cost ~ $0.042 / 1k, weighted acc ~86.0%. Means we can hit near-baseline accuracy with ~7% lower cost vs 13b-only, and ~7% higher cost vs 9b-fp16-only.

marta: Key failure modes for int8: factual hallucinations on long context (>800 tokens), numerical conversions in finance prompts, and occasional truncation on very long outputs. Int4 increases hallucination rate noticeably.

marta: Perf notes: int8 reduces p50 reliably but p95 still dominated by KV-cache miss + large context cases. We saw a small jitter due to kernel fallback on some GPU drivers (tracked in #PR 4823).

marta: Recommendation options: 1) Default to int8 for GTN canary (big cost wins), add 13b-fp16 fallback for low-confidence responses; 2) Keep fp16 for canary to minimize product risk, run longer int8 A/B; 3) Use int4 in isolated low-latency microservices only (not GTN).

marta: Asking product/ops: which risk profile do we take for the initial GTN rollout? If we go int8 default, ops: need canary plan + dedicated pool + fast rollback metric.

jordan: Thanks — nice summary. Quick Q: that 1.1pp drop for int8 is on our full GTN-CORE eval or just auto metrics? We need human-rated accuracy on the 1k high-value subset.

marta: jordan: auto eval is the number above. We ran a 500-sample human spot-check: int8 human pass=88/100 vs fp16=90/100 (same direction, small sample). I'll queue a 1k human eval next.

kai: From routing POV, suggest confidence threshold on softmax-avg or token-entropy to gate fallback. Also consider route-by-prefill-length: >800 tokens -> 13b. We already have the instrumentation to try this latency-aware filter.

lee: Ops note: GPU kernels — the p95 jitter for int8 appears on our 530 drivers. PR 4823 pins a newer cu kernel that reduced jitter in bench. If we plan int8 default, please include driver rollout and benchmark before canary. Also recommend dedicated node pool to avoid noisy neighbors.

ana: Product: GTN cares most about correctness on money/legal flows. If int8 shows systematic numerical issues, we should default those routes to 13b regardless of cost. Can we tag flows and opt them out automatically?

marta: ana: yes — we can add tag-based routing. We already have a rule engine prototype: tag -> route. I'll add money/legal as explicit opt-out for int8 until human eval passes.

jordan: Action items I see: (1) Run 1k human eval stratified by flow (finance/legal/longform) — marta to own. (2) Ops to stage kernel + driver fix on a small dedicated pool + run perf smoke — lee. (3) Implement confidence-based fallback rule prototype and simulate traffic today — kai. (4) Decide canary default (int8 vs fp16) by EOD Friday — product + eng.

ops-bot: Canary slot requested: eng-ml-dedicated-pool request queued for 2025-08-14T09:00Z (canary-id: canary-20250814-03).

marta: I'll post the 1k eval plan (sampling strata + rubric) in this thread by EOD. If everyone OK, I'll start the canary playbook after ops confirms the driver patch smoke results. :thumbsup:
